newsitem.title: CHINA: China shuts down 50,000 polluting factories.
newsitem.headline: China shuts down 50,000 polluting factories.

text.p: China, which strengthened its policy on protecting the environment in the midst of rapid economic growth, has shut down nearly 50,000 severely polluting enterprises since August, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

The enterprises were engaged in gold mining, coking, tanning, paper making, oil refining, electric coating, lead and zinc mining or sulphur extraction, an official of the State Bureau for Environmental Protection was quoted as saying.
About 92 percent of paper mills blacklisted for pollution had been shut down or had suspended production, Xinhua said.

More than 20,000 environment officials fanned out across China to inspect factories and close down polluting ones after the State Council, or cabinet, issued an edict in August to step up environmental protection.
"The closure of the enterprises has had no serious impact on local economies," the official said.
Most of the factory workers were local farmers or transient labourers, the official said.

China's environmental problems have worsened over the past decade with the economy's rapid development. Some of the world's highest levels of air pollution have been recorded by Chinese cities and acid rain is common.
Rivers and lakes across China are lined with tens of thousands of factories, many of which have little or no waste water treatment facilities.
